newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices tumble to their lowest since September.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices tumble to their lowest since September.

text.p: Oil prices tumbled on Thursday to trade below $22 a barrel for the first time in four months and traders said weakness in the heating oil market was pulling the entire energy complex down.

At 1505 GMT, world benchmark Brent Blend crude futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) shed 77 cents to trade at a low of $21.70 a barrel, the lowest level for front-month crude since September 23.
Much of the fall came during the afternoon session after the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) opened and where heating oil futures broke through several layers of support.
"The heating oil season is over," a New York dealer said. March heating oil on NYMEX had its lowest settlement in five months on Wednesday and the London market usually takes its lead from New York.

Crude oil futures have resiliently held support at the psychological $22 a barrel floor in recent days and failed to break through on Tuesday, despite evidence that gas oil futures were no longer providing a winter prop to the rest of the barrel.
Weekly U.S. oil stocks data issued on Tuesday and Wednesday showed that industry inventories were in surplus compared with year-ago levels for the first time since June 1995.
IPE gas oil -- used in Europe for heating -- led the way in early London business. February gas oil was $9 a tonne lower in the afternoon at $192.00 a tonne.

"We've had some weakness in gas oil. But I wouldn't over analyse this and I wouldn't call it a break -- the volume is far too little," one trader said. "No one really knows what's going on other than the market looks weak."

Signs that the market was well-supplied also gave the bears the upper hand. A Reuters survey showed January production by members of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) rose 300,000 barrels per day (bpd), swollen by Iraq's first full month of exports under the United Nations oil-for-food deal.
Wellhead crude oil production from OPEC countries rose to 26.64 million bpd from a revised 26.34 million in December, a Reuter survey of oil analysts, OPEC delegates and company officials found.

And OPEC, pumping an extra 600,000 bpd in the past two months, looks set to add more barrels as foreign companies, bringing new fields onstream, seek to cash in on their investments, OPEC monitors said.
"I see OPEC heading to 27 million bpd by the middle of the year -- easily," said Mehdi Varzi, director of research for energy at finance house Kleinwort Benson Securities.
OPEC's official output ceiling is a combined 25.033 million bpd for the 11-member cartel.
